text: 8-week resistance training program while consuming either a ketogenic diet (~42 g carbohydrate/day) or nonketogenic diet (~55% of total calories from carbohydrate); protein intake was equated between conditions (2 g/ kg/day) and both groups were individually supervised by a nutritionist. Results showed that the nonketogenic group gained 1.3 kg (2.9 lb) of lean mass while the ketogenic diet group showed a slight decrease. These findings are consistent with those of Kephart and colleagues
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
